contributions.statement: Search or pick one workflow per task type offline and serve it to every request rather than searching a workflow per incoming request: per-request search returned workflows costing 1.1-11.6x the tokens and 1.1-6.6x the sequential calls per problem with no better best-case quality, and it overfit the request's own paraphrases.
contributions.evidence: §5 / Table 5, six benchmarks, same base model and search budget: query-level vs task-level inference cost (e.g. SWE-Bench 115.3k vs 102.7k tokens, 7.36 vs 6.53 calls; MBPP 20.1k vs 2.1k tokens); rho_HV as low as 0.28 vs >=0.66, though the two modes use different held-out notions (audit). Fig. 6 compares the best value over 11 served workflows per mode, a max-over-set (audit). Echoes Wang et al. 2026b.
relative_to: 2606.22902 static best-per-task-category table performs about as well as an LLM router
Wang et al. 2026b: a few top-ranked task-level workflows cover as many queries as a per-query generator

contributions.statement: When certifying an LLM workflow, measure paraphrase robustness and repeated-run consistency as separate checks, since one did not reliably predict the other outside code repair.
contributions.evidence: §4 Objectives and metrics: correlation between robustness and consistency over 132 served workflows is 0.63 overall, ranging from -0.13 on GPQA to 0.87 on SWE-Bench; for code repair the two tracked closely, so the gain for a coding team is limited.
relative_to: 2608.11386 measure repeated-run consistency (pass^k), not only pass rate

reason: The Pareto-search method itself is a benchmark contribution, but its side-by-side of per-request versus per-task workflow search gives a measured cost penalty for generating workflows per request, which bears directly on whether to let a planner emit a fresh DAG per ticket.
